title: Orchestrated breaker hysteresis with safe routing and staged shedder
creator: Maya Hargrove
description:
Problem: We currently have brittle, single-threshold breakers per service that either allow noisy tenants to take down models or immediately route large cohorts to lower-quality fallbacks. This causes SLO breaches in primary regions and unpredictable customer experiences during partial outages.

Proposal: Implement an orchestrated breaker system that composes per-dependency, per-model, and per-tenant breakers into a cascading decision graph with hysteresis windows and staged safe routing. Key ideas:
- Multi-tier trip thresholds: fast short-window trip (1m error rate or latency p99), medium window (5-15m) and slow window (1hr) to avoid oscillation.
- Hysteresis: after a trip, enforce a cool-down plus progressive recovery: allow X% traffic back every Y minutes when health metrics improve.
- Per-tenant shaping: tenants with higher priority keep higher headroom; low-tier tenants can be shed earlier. Headroom computed from tokenized rate and p50/p99 latency budgets.
- Model-aware fallback mapping: map each primary model to a ranked list of compatible fallback variants (quantized lower-cost model, regional replica, or cached-prefix path). Each fallback carries a degradation budget (max allowed quality drop) and capacity footprint metadata.
- Safety gates: any fallback decision must preserve privacy constraints (no cross-tenant crossover for private deployments) and respect region/geo restrictions.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Decision graph vs. centralized controller: We prefer a distributed graph with local fast-path evaluation to avoid control-plane latency. A lightweight global policy pushes thresholds and fallback ranking; nodes evaluate locally against streaming metrics. Trade-off: slight policy propagation lag vs. huge improvements in local failover speed.
- Conservative recovery policy to avoid rapid thrash. This can delay full capacity restoration but prevents repeated SLO flaps.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Implement local circuit evaluator that considers (tenant_priority, model_variant, dep_latency_p99, dep_error_rate) and emits one of {pass, shed, fallback-variant, regional-reroute}.
2) Add hysteresis config (short/medium/long windows) and progressive recovery parameters to policy store; default values: short=1m (trigger if errors>5% or p99>1.5x SLO), medium=10m, long=1h; recovery step=10% traffic every 5 minutes if metrics move inside threshold.
3) Ensure fallback mapping is configurable per model and enforced during canary.
4) End-to-end tests: simulation harness that fuzzes errors/latency and demonstrates reduced SLO breach count vs. baseline under two outage scenarios (regional spike, model degradation).
5) Observability: add dashboard panels for breaker state transitions, per-tenant shed rates, fallback invocation counts, and end-to-end error budget burn.

Rollout plan:
- Phase A (dev & infra): build evaluator + policy store + simulator (2 weeks).
- Phase B (stage canary): enable on 5% of traffic for internal tenants, compare SLI curves for 24h. Add logs/trace hooks (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/9876).
- Phase C (prod phased): 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 2 weeks, with automated rollback on >2x SLO burn compared to baseline.

Testing:
- Unit: evaluator logic, hysteresis windows, recovery stepping.
- Integration: connect to metrics stream and verify local decision matches golden policy.
- Chaos: simulate dependency slowdowns in a multi-region testbed.

Metrics to monitor:
- Primary SLOs: p50/p99 latency, error rate, end-to-end availability by region.
- Breaker metrics: trip-rate, avg time-in-tripped-state, recovery-step-count, percent traffic diverted to each fallback.
- Customer metrics: top-10 tenants by shed rate and churn-risk indicators.

Notes / Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/Orchestrated+Breaker+Design
- Simulator repo: https://github.com/redwood/reliability-sim/tree/feature/orchestrated-breaker
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/9876
- Related tickets: ENG-41209, ENG-21045

Open questions:
1) Do we default to fallback model with quantized weights or to regional replica? Depends on quality budget — need PM input.
2) Should low-priority tenants have opt-out for fallbacks that materially change output semantics? Likely yes, expose tenant-level policy.
3) Cost accounting: how do we ensure fallbacks that increase cost are charged appropriately to tenants? Connect with billing team for per-fallback metering.
